segments.title: THE CHART THAT GOES BLANK
segments.angle: Imagine this idea has been implemented and failed spectacularly one year from now. What are the most likely reasons for its failure? How could we mitigate those risks now?

sources.text: Consistency Compounds Exponentially: Allowing your consistency to break sets you back magnitudes more than you could ever imagine.
Staying On Your Purpose: Spend at least 1 hour a day doing what you feel you're meant to do, now.
Staying On Your Purpose: Don't wait any longer.

Consistency Compounds Exponentially: Every time you choose to do something other than following your routine, you've just nipped your opportunity for compounding growth at its bud, before it's even had a chance to grow.
Staying On Your Purpose: Don't believe the myth that "one day, things will be different". They won't.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: In the small hours the kettle's ticking up toward the boil. Your eyes land on the mug on its tile. You'll start properly tomorrow, and the purpose note has a name for that sentence: a myth. Here it comes anyway.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Most people think a missed day is just a missed day. One slipped session, one bad week, and the plan's still in the drawer, barely dented. I'd have believed that too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Barely dented? The note hears the first crack in a dam. A slip is never only a slip, March. It is the opening, and the water does not wait for permission.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: So you're saying one missed morning is how the whole plan falls over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Almost. The missed hour is only the crack. What brings the wall down is the story you tell afterward. The note puts it plainly: 'Allowing your consistency to break sets you back magnitudes more than you could ever imagine.' The best of what it says about the story I am keeping back for later.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: So the hour itself is nothing. It's what you decide the day after.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Precisely. The hour is nothing. The sum you were building is everything, and you were the one who allowed it to break.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Fair. Anyway, the mug.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Let's say it's a year from now and the plan's dead.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dead already? How swift.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Autopsy time. The routine was an hour before the kettle, set for a good morning. Then a cold morning arrives, the hour's impossible, and you stay under the blanket.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Next day you open the chart. There's a gap in it. The streak's broken, so why bother. The kettle stays cold, and the brass key goes back in the wrong pocket.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Laziness, March. Plain idleness. The man simply could not be bothered.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Could he? Or did one gap make the whole plan look like a lie? From outside it's idleness. From inside it looks finished, so there's no point.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A romantic reading. Lazy men have always had better stories.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Ha. Please.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: So what would the stool have been that day? Not the full hour. A kettle and one try at the key. One foot, one try at the lock.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A pitiful gesture. A stool is no match for a streak already broken.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: It's the only thing keeping the run alive.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sentimental, and quite dreadful.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now, March, I must ask what you hid in the design. You keep a part of yourself out of the room. I have a theory. The moth on the lamp. You are the moth, drawn in and sure to singe. Yes?

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: No, the moth is nowhere near...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the loose coat-hook screw. You are that screw, always working free of the wall just when...

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Wrong. And you're hunting for a rule.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The dimmer, then. A secret switch that lowers you when no one is looking.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Nope. You're enjoying this far too much.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Enjoying? I am enduring a long, dreary list of refusals. Must you rule them out one by one, March? It is dreadfully long.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Guilty, and you're still guessing.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: You keep guessing, and I keep knocking them down. Here's why it matters. You just built a plan with a hidden part, sitting where nobody checks. That's how a routine fails too. Quietly, somewhere nobody's looking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Very well. Quiet failures, both of them, and I concede that much.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Now set the purpose note beside it. 'Spend at least 1 hour a day doing what you feel you're meant to do, now.' And the blunt one: 'Don't wait any longer.'

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: The consistency note says never let the chain break. The purpose note says do the hour now. Side by side, they catch each other out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Go on. What do they catch?

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: A trap. An all or nothing streak makes one missed day feel like ruin, and ruin is the easiest excuse to quit. So you wait for a perfect week, and the perfect week never shows up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the chain itself is the snare. Never break it, and any break becomes a verdict.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Yes. The safe version is the smallest one you can keep on a bad day. Not the full hour. The stool.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Neither note shows that alone. One demands a perfect record, the other demands action now. Only together do they admit the perfect record is what kills the action.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: So imagine someone who believes the all or nothing version. Their streak chart goes blank after a cold dawn, and they're left with a shelf of unopened plans, waiting for a clean restart that never comes.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Now the other one. Someone who believes the stool version. The same cold morning, and they moved the stool a foot. A try at the lock. The chart keeps going, and the gap is only a gap.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the best of the purpose note I keep for the next round, and you will not enjoy it, March.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: I've got a comeback saved for later. It isn't kind, and you'll hear it when you're not braced.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Here's where I land. What broke the plan was the story told about the missed hour, the blank square that made the whole chart look finished.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the stool was the plan all along, and I offer J the title Keeper of the Unfinished Chart, in its honour.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: No. But you're right about the stool. Now the mug, which I'm moving an inch as we speak.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Up next, the rest of the chain and the purpose note, where the nasty bit lives.
